Information Chosen Against the Family

Source: R/information.R
auto_info.Rd

Selects an information that statmod() settles once the family is known. It is the default of the argument inner_information of statmod(), and reml() and ml() accept it as well.

In inner_information, the expected information is chosen where the family writes it exactly and at an acceptable cost, and the observed information otherwise. With iwls(), a run on the expected information continues on the observed information as soon as Fisher scoring contracts the score slowly, and a run on the observed information takes the step on the expected information where the repaired observed step finds no acceptable point. With an optimizers7 optimizer the settled matrix is the Hessian that the optimizer receives. In reml() and ml() the expected information is chosen for a Student t, a skew t or a Cauchy response (wrapped or not), whose observed information is not positive definite at an outlier, and the observed information is chosen for every other family. The fitted model records the settled choice.

aic(), bic() and the variance objects bayesian_vcov(), frequentist_vcov() and unconditional_vcov() do not accept it, since the quantity that each of them computes is defined on one named matrix. information_objects compares the three information objects.

Usage

auto_info(method = NULL, repair_floor = 1e-08)

Arguments

method

NULL (the default) or an object that inherits from distributions7::ExpectMethod; it is used as the method of the distributions7::expected_info() that the settled choice or the fallback selects:

  • NULL: the closed form of the family where it has one, and distributions7::expect_opg() otherwise;

  • distributions7::expect_opg(): the outer product of the observed scores, which costs one gradient;

  • distributions7::expect_integrate(): quadrature (or summation over the support), with identity = "hessian" or identity = "score";

  • distributions7::expect_mc(): Monte Carlo.

An object is used also for a family that has the closed form. distributions7::expected_derivative_methods compares the methods. Any other value signals an error.

repair_floor

A single positive number. A penalized observed information whose smallest eigenvalue is below repair_floor times the largest absolute eigenvalue is read as indefinite by iwls(). The step on it then floors the eigenvalues (the floor of the solver, see solve_chol()), the expected information takes the step only if the search on the repaired matrix fails, and a run on it does not take the extra step that follows convergence. The default is 1e-8. The argument is read by iwls() only.

Value

An S7 object of class AutoInfo, which inherits from distributions7::Information, with the properties method and repair_floor.

See also

distributions7::observed_info() and distributions7::expected_info() for the objects that name a matrix; information_objects for the comparison; distributions7::expected_derivative_methods for the methods; AutoInfo for the class; statmod(), iwls(), reml() and ml() for the functions that take the object.

Examples

auto_info()
#> Information chosen against the family (closed form where the family has one, otherwise the outer product of the scores)
auto_info(method = distributions7::expect_integrate(identity = "score"),
          repair_floor = 1e-10)
#> Information chosen against the family (expectation by integration against the density (identity = score))

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(120, -2, 2))
dd$y <- sin(1.4 * dd$x) + rnorm(120, sd = 0.3)
G <- distributions7::gaussian1_distrib()
fit <- statmod(y ~ s(x, bspline_smooth(k = 8)), G, dd,
               inner_information = auto_info(),
               outer_criterion = reml(information = auto_info()))
fit@methods$smooth
#> iwls: qr, expected information (the observed after 10 iterations)
#>   maxit 1000, tol 1e-06
